{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Ivan Maurice Roitt''' (born 30 September 1927) is a British scientist. He was educated at [[King Edward's School, Birmingham]] and [[Balliol College]], [[Oxford University]]. He was Head of the Department of Immunology at [[University College London]] from 1967 to 1992, and is currently Honorary Director of the Centre for Investigative & Diagnostic Oncology at [[Middlesex University]], London.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rsm.ac.uk/welcom/council/ivan-roitt.php/ |title=Professor Ivan M. Roitt - the Royal Society of Medicine |access-date=2014-04-08 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616042519/http://www.rsm.ac.uk/welcom/council/ivan-roitt.php |archive-date=2013-06-16 }} Royal Society of Medicine</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Our research {{!}} Middlesex University London |url=https://www.mdx.ac.uk/our-research |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=www.mdx.ac.uk}}</ref>

In 1956, together with [[Deborah Doniach]] and Peter Campbell, he made the classic discovery of [[thyroglobulin]] [[autoantibodies]] in [[Hashimoto's thyroiditis]] which helped to open the whole concept of a relationship between [[Autoimmune diseases|autoimmunity]] and human disease.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brostoff |first=Jonathan |date=2004-01-15 |title=Obituary: Deborah Doniach |url=http://www.theguardian.com/society/2004/jan/15/health.obituaries |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref> The work was extended to an intensive study of autoimmune phenomena in [[pernicious anemia]] and primary biliary [[cirrhosis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rsm.ac.uk/welcom/council/ivan-roitt.php/ |title=Professor Ivan M. Roitt - the Royal Society of Medicine |access-date=2014-04-08 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616042519/http://www.rsm.ac.uk/welcom/council/ivan-roitt.php |archive-date=2013-06-16 }} Royal Society of Medicine</ref>

In 1983 he was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]], and has been elected to Honorary Membership of the [[Royal College of Physicians]] and appointed Honorary Fellow of The [[Royal Society of Medicine]]. He was awarded the [[Gairdner Foundation International Award]] in 1964.
He is an honorary member of the [[British Society for Immunology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.immunology.org/about-us/our-people/our-members/honorary-members|title=Honorary members &#124; British Society for Immunology}}</ref>
